newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Emperor seeks international gold buys.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Emperor seeks international gold buys.

text.p: Fiji gold miner Emperor Mines Ltd said on Monday it was on track to meet its profit forecast in the first six months of 1996/97 and was on the lookout for international acquisitions along with investor Robert Friedland.
The company also said its net profit in the first quarter ended September 30 was A$428,000. No comparisons were given.
Emperor said the quarterly result incuded a A$563,000 profit from hedging and a charge of A$710,000 for the write-off of half its exploration costs.
"Although the last quarter production was down on expectations, the half year result is expected to be on target," the company said.
"Profit will be down compared to plan if the current gold price continues," he said.
The company, which operates the Vatukoula mine in Fiji, said it was looking at joint ventures or merger opportunities in the Pacific, central and Southeast Asia, and Australia.

"The key criteria for any new opportunities to be considered are resources with a potential minimum of one million ounces, and a clear indication that Emperor's management skills will add significant value to the new business," it said.

"In the search for investment opportunities, the company aims to capitalise on its relationships within the international investment community and with prominent mining identities, to take advantage of EML's position of strength," it said.

"International mining financier Robert Friedland and chairman of Indochina Goldfields which owns a 16 percent stake in the company, has been closely linked to the company's initial investigations overseas as has Emperor's chairman, Tan Sri Azmi Wan Hamzah, who is a leading businessman in the Southeast Asia region."
